verses.saheeh: I do not worship what you worship.
verses.khattab: I do not worship what you worship
verses.jalalayn: I do not worship, at present, what you worship, of idols,
verses.romanUrdu: Main unki ibadat nahin karta jinki ibadat tum karte ho

verses.saheeh: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.
verses.khattab: nor do you worship what I worship
verses.jalalayn: and you do not worship, at present, what I worship, and that is God, exalted be He, alone,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur na tum uski ibadat karne wale ho jiski ibadat mai karta hoon

verses.saheeh: Nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship.
verses.khattab: I will never worship what you worship
verses.jalalayn: nor will I worship, in the future, what you have worshipped,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur na mai unki ibadat karne wala hoon jinki ibadat tum ne ki hai

verses.indopak: وَ لَاۤ اَنۡـتُمۡ عٰبِدُوۡنَ مَاۤ اَعۡبُدُ ؕ
verses.saheeh: Nor will you be worshippers of what I worship.
verses.khattab: nor will you ever worship what I worship
verses.jalalayn: nor will you worship, in the future, what I worship: God knew that they would never become believers (the use of [the inanimate] mā, ‘what’, to refer to God is meant to counter [the reference to ‘what thing’ they worship]).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur na tum uski ibadat karne waley ho jiski ibadat main karta hoon

verses.saheeh: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."
verses.khattab: You have your way, and I have my Way.”
verses.jalalayn: You have your religion, idolatry, and I have a religion’, Islam: this was [revealed] before he was commanded to wage war [against the idolaters] (all seven Qur'anic readers omit the yā’ of the genitive possessive construction [in wa-liya dīni] whether with a pause or without; Ya‘qūb, however, retains it in both cases).
verses.romanUrdu: Tumhare liye tumhara deen hai aur mere liye mera deen
